newsitem.title: USA: CNS Inc prepares to launch new product.
newsitem.headline: CNS Inc prepares to launch new product.

text.p: CNS Inc, developer of the Breathe Right nasal strip, said Monday it is preparing to roll out a new patch to treat pain, while continuing tests on another product to help allergy sufferers.
In a conference call with industry analysts, CNS officials said the new TheraPatch product will initially account for only a small percentage of sales in the first quarter of 1997.
TheraPatch is a transdermal analgesic developed by LecTec Corp and licensed to CNS.

"It's still going to take some time to get (TheraPatch) out on the shelf," said CNS President Rick Jahnke, "unless you want to spend a bazillion dollars (on advertising) and that's not the way we do things."
Jahnke said the other product currently being tested is called Allergel, a gel that is applied around the nose that repels pollen electrostatically. The gel is colorless and odorless once it dries.

"Allergel is still in development in early clinical trials," Jahnke said. "We're ready to begin the second round of clinical trials, but we can't predict the timing of when it will reach the market until we see the results of the trials."
Another CNS official told Reuters that Allergel was originally expected to reach the consumer market by the fall of 1997 or the spring of 1998 at the earliest.

CNS earlier Monday reported sales of $24.6 million in the fourth quarter of 1996 ended December 31, compared to sales of $12.1 million one year ago. Net income in the period totaled $5.5 million, versus $2.9 million in the year-ago quarter.
When asked about the $62.4 million in cash and securities on hand at the end of the fiscal year, Jahnke said CNS is preparing to invest in its manufacturing operations.
"We will be integrating certain manufacturing operations, and we have to do a major upgrade to our information systems as we go online with a number of major retailers," he said.
"That will allow us to understand their sell-through data specifically and manage the inventory at the store level," Jahnke said.
Jahnke added that the company will also consider acquiring certain compatible product lines, although he said there were no deals pending in the immediate future.
